title.narrative: Assistance d'urgence par transferts monétaires aux victimes des inondations en Guinée.

description.narrative: Between August 3 and October 1, 2024, flooding affected more than 175,000 people, including 2,834 pregnant women, 5,115 breastfeeding women, 1,258 people with reduced mobility, 7,220 elderly people, 15,374 school children, and 869 displaced households. This represents a more than tenfold increase compared to the same period in 2023. Eighteen of the country's thirty-three prefectures were affected. The National Agency for Emergency and Humanitarian Disaster Management (ANGUCH), responsible for managing and coordinating responses to humanitarian emergencies, reported that so far, only 14,000 out of 175,000 people in four prefectures (Coyah, Forécariah, Kouroussa, and Kindia) have received initial emergency assistance. The priority needs identified are food security, health, education and WASH (water, sanitation and hygiene). To respond to this crisis, the Government of Guinea, in collaboration with the United Nations system, has developed an emergency response plan. Faced with the imminent needs in these crucial sectors, the Resident Coordinator (RC) requested the CERF allocation to implement an emergency response aimed at improving the living conditions of people not covered by initial assistance. This assistance consists of providing mobile money transfers for 30 days to beneficiaries in the prefectures of Gueckedou and Mandiana. The food program, in its mandate to provide emergency food security assistance, aims to contribute to the efforts of the government and other humanitarian actors. With the CERF fund, it is a question of responding quickly to the food and non-food needs of populations who have lost their food stocks, livestock, homes and agricultural fields. The use of the CERF fund will complement the assistance already provided with the IRA funds in Mandiana, one of the most affected areas, and will extend assistance to Guéckédou where the IRA fund does not intervene. The IRA fund covers 30 days of rations in the areas of Kouroussa, Mandiana and Kankan. The cash transfer modality was chosen as the most appropriate to assist the victims. This transfer will allow victims to have more autonomy in the use of assistance and to meet their non-food needs. As part of this initiative, WFP has developed a distribution plan based on the 11,806 households identified, representing 70,836 beneficiaries according to ANGUCH, including 9,668 children aged 6 to 59 months, 905 pregnant and lactating women, and 200 people with reduced mobility. The plan provides for a total allocation of USD 1,325,000 over a period of three to six months. WFP plans to transfer USD 79 to each household, less withdrawal fees, to cover their basic needs. This amount will be distributed in Guinean francs according to the rate of the month of distribution.
